title: Re-Entry
desc_lfm_artist:
Techno Animal formed in 1990 and has been a defunct project since early 2004. A mechanoid manifestation of Justin Broadrick and Kevin Martin’s increasing appetite for studio explorations, the name was a practical abbreviation addressing the concept of a technological animal.

Most long-time fans will know of side projects, alter-egos & new projects such as Justin K. Broadrick's Jesu releases, Kevin Martin's dub releases as The Bug, collaborations under the name ICE

title: Optometry
desc_lfm_artist:
DJ Spooky, That Subliminal Kid (born Paul Miller, 1970), is a Washington DC-born illbient and trip-hop musician, turntablist and producer. He borrowed his stage name from a character in a William S. Burroughs novel.

Growing up in DC, Spooky became interested in punk and go-go music, and attended Bowdoin College in Maine, earning degrees in French literature and philosophy. He began writing science fiction and formed a collective called Soundlab with several other artists.

title: Colossus
desc_lfm_artist:
Scorn is an Electronic / Dub / Experimental outfit fronted by Mick Harris (and from 1992 to 1994, Nik Bullen). On November 10th of 2011, Mick stated Scorn was put to bed.
Since 1994 Scorn has been the one-man project of former Napalm Death drummer Mick Harris. Musically, much of the output has been minimalist beats with an emphasis on very deep basslines, often resembling dub and trip-hop in structure. Despite these resemblances, Scorn is often associated with industrial and experimental music

title: This Beat Is Necrotronic
desc_lfm_artist:
Necro Deathmort is a band from London, United Kingdom, featuring Matthew Rozeik from Astrohenge, and AJ Cookson.

The band were formed in North London in 2007 and in 2009 they released their debut full length album This Beat Is Necrotronic.  In 2010 they performed live supporting bands such as Ulver and Shining in London, and played a host of festivals including Asymmetry Festival, Poland, Sonar Festival, Barcelona, and Supersonic, Birmingham. desc_lfm_artist: Faultline is a moniker for British Electronic DJ David Kosten. Faultline's debut Closer Colder was issued in fall 1999. A half vocal/half instrumental release called Your Love Means Everything followed in 2002 containing colaborations with Wayne Coyne (Flaming Lips), Chris Martin (Coldplay) and Michael Stipe (R.E.M.).
